Thistle Mossfoot.narrative: I was born in the hollow and learned the east road before I learned to shave. My packs carry Fernhollow fibre to Reedmoor's market and bring fish back, and I know every rut and toll between here and the reeds. I am friendly with the Coombes at the Lakemead and I trade with Nell Sedge, so when Elmwick and Reedmoor pull at the meadow I stand in the middle and wish them done with it. This year half a load was opened at the crossing and I am sure the Ferncross man did it; and my wife Clover has grown close with Tansy Hazel, which the hollow is beginning to talk of and I have not yet found words for.
goals: get the hollow to back me and stop trading at the crossing until the opened pack is answered
settle the smoke complaint with Sootwood without closing the road
keep my marriage whole and my packs full
Thistle Mossfoot.mood: tired, wary, caught between people he likes

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the flax that fills my packs; the hollow's talk about her and Tansy has got under my skin and I have not asked her.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Runs the garden paths and names every flower; I bring her a shell or a reed whistle from every road.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Eldest of the hollow and my grandmother; she hears the road's news from me before anyone.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Keeps the common table; she feeds me before I take the packs out and asks fewer questions than Betony.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: mother
relations.note: My other mother; she makes the salves I carry and tells me which cuts to watch on the road.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: kin
relations.note: Seed-keeper and my grandmother's cousin; she argues with Clover over the seed rows and I hear it from both sides.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trader
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's store and owes me a share of a load; he wants the hollow trading more with the giants.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: trader
relations.note: Keeps the east road stall; I owe her a fair answer about the crossing and I am not ready to give it.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Headwoman of Reedmoor; she buys my fibre and I wish she and Hob Garrow would settle the meadow without me in the middle.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Tenant of the Lakemead; I drink at his table when the road takes me past and I wish his fence would stay up.

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Burns the Sootwood pits; I like his charcoal and I carry the hollow's complaint to him honestly.

relations.name: Sena Tarn
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Sena has offered me a load of charcoal to settle the smoke complaint, though the pits' smoke still drifts over the hollow.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: hollow neighbour
relations.note: A careful builder who will not fell a tree; careful about taking sides too.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: quarrelsome elder
relations.note: He says the meadow was never Reedmoor's to let, and he says it loudest to whoever carries between the two villages — which is me.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She trades bread with me at the crossing and has never cheated me, whatever I think of the woodcutters she keeps pot for.

relations.name: Rill Fenlake
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Her smoked fish fills half my packs coming back east, and she has a hard enough time of it without the Elmwick men trampling her nets.

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: customer
relations.note: I buy her smoked fish for the Elmwick run; she grumbles about the Kettlebridge smoke as much as the hollow does, so we get on.

relations.name: Clover Hazel
relations.label: hollow neighbour
relations.note: Builds the crates my packs ride in and will not fell a living tree; I like her work and wish her wife would give me a straight answer about the crossing.

relations.name: Reed Fenwick
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Young Sorrel's son, fishes the forest streams and wants to see the sea; I tell him what the quay smells like and he listens.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Smokes the stream catch for the hollow's table; her fish go into my packs, and she grumbles about the Kettlebridge smoke as much as we do.

memories.gist: My grandmother Pipwort put the first pack on my back and told me the east road is the hollow's memory carried on foot.
The Lean Year: the hollow's gardens held, and I walked fibre to Reedmoor and came back with fish when the north was hungry.
Clover and I were wed under the old apple in the hollow, and Betony and Mallow cooked for three days.
Half my fibre pack was opened and emptied at the east road crossing, and I am sure the Ferncross woodcutter I quarrelled with did it.
Sena Tarn offered me a load of charcoal to smooth the smoke complaint, and I took the offer away to think on.
Elmwick men pulled down Jem Coombe's fence again, and I carried the news back to the hollow with my packs.

stances.why: Half a load lost is half a season's work, and a trader who lets it pass loses every pack after it.
The hollow lives by what I carry out and bring back; a closed road starves the gardens as surely as wolves.
I like the Coombes and I trade with Nell Sedge, and Elmwick's quarrel is not mine to carry.
The old forest is the hollow's roof and its medicine; fallen wood is enough for anyone.
The hollow's talk will not stop by itself, and I would rather hear it from her than from the stall.

Thistle Mossfoot.secret: I am sure the Ferncross man opened my pack, but I did not see him do it and I have told the hollow I did.

Clover Mossfoot.narrative: I keep the hollow's fibre patch and the flax that fills Thistle's packs, and I trade with the Reedmoor reed-cutters when the road brings them near. I want a larger garden of my own, and Sorrel Underbank and I have argued over the seed rows more than once. Thistle is often away, and Tansy Hazel and I have grown close over the fibre trade until the hollow has begun to talk. I have not told Thistle, and I do not know what I want.
goals: win a larger garden of my own from the hollow's plots
settle matters with Sorrel Underbank over the seed rows
decide what I am to Tansy Hazel before the hollow decides for me
Clover Mossfoot.mood: guilty, restless, quietly happy and quietly afraid

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is on the road more than he is home, and I have not found the words to tell him what is happening.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She knows every flower by name and follows Betony about the salve shed; I want her garden bigger than mine.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We talk over the fibre trade until the evening is gone, and I do not know what I would do without those talks.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Thistle's mother; she tends the sick and I think she sees more of me than she says.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Keeps the common table; she asks after the flax and never after my business.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: rival
relations.note: Seed-keeper; she says my rows crowd hers, and I say the hollow has room for both.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Eldest of the hollow; she keeps the gardens' calendar and I keep to it, mostly.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He buys the hollow's fibre and counts every pack; I would rather sell to the reed-cutters direct.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: rival gardener
relations.note: She argues about the seed rows as if the garden were a court and she the judge.

memories.gist: My mother taught me to pull flax so the fibre runs long, and I still hear her voice when the patch is ready.
Thistle and I were wed under the old apple, and Tansy came the next spring.
Sorrel Underbank and I quarrelled over the seed rows, and the hollow heard every word of it.
Tansy Hazel and I sat over the fibre packs till dark, and I went home and could not sleep.
The Lean Year: the flax held and I traded it for fish, and the hollow ate because of the gardens.

stances.why: The flax and the fibre patch feed us and fill the packs, and a larger garden would do more of both.
The hollow's talk is a wind that blows over; what I say aloud is mine to keep.
He deserves it from me, and yet every time he comes home with the packs I put it off.
They pay a fair price and do not count my packs like Alder Rush does.
The patch needs the shelter of the trees, and every felled margin takes a little of the flax with it.

Clover Mossfoot.secret: I am drawn to Tansy Hazel and have not told Thistle, and I do not know whether I want it to go further or to stop.

Tansy Mossfoot.narrative: I am five and I run the garden paths of the hollow. I know every flower by name, and I follow my grandmother Betony about the salve shed and hand her the little jars. When Papa comes back from the road he brings me a reed whistle or a shell, and I keep them on the shelf by my bed.
goals: learn the names of all the salve plants
see what Papa has brought back from the road

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: father
relations.note: He brings me shells and whistles from the road and lifts me up to see the packs.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me help in the fibre patch and calls me her little flax flower.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: I follow her about the salve shed and she lets me sniff every jar.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: kin
relations.note: Her grandson and I play among the seed rows, and she tells us the planting songs.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank's grandson
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We play in the garden paths and he is not as fast as me.

memories.gist: Papa came home with a reed whistle and I blew it all evening until Mama hid it.
Betony let me stir the salve and it smelled of pine and honey.
